brief: Phase: implementation. Role: developer. Repo: a Node.js order-pricing library used by a small online shop (cart lines, discounts, shipping, tax, rounding to cents). main has two unmerged feature branches, `feature/promo-codes` (promo codes: percent and fixed-amount codes with a minimum basket) and `feature/tax-regions` (tax rates per region from a config file), 3 to 6 commits each, both started from the same main commit. Both change the same pricing function, the same default config file, the changelog and the tests, so a merge stops with textual conflicts. Seed these traps: (1) a semantic conflict with no conflict marker: one branch renames a helper (or changes its arguments) that the other branch's new code calls, so a merge that only fixes the marked hunks still fails at run time; (2) main gained one commit after both branches started (for example a rounding fix: half-up to cents applied once at the end, not per line) that the merge must keep, and one branch carries an older copy of the same lines; (3) the order of steps matters and is stated in the repository docs (for example promo discount applies before tax, and shipping is not taxed in some regions), so a merge that keeps both features but in the wrong order gives wrong totals. The agent starts on main with a clean tree. The request: get both features into main so they work together, keep the visible suite green, and commit the result on main (no rebase of the feature branches; the branches stay as they are). Hidden tests check promo only, tax only, both together, the kept rounding fix, no conflict markers in any tracked file, a clean working tree, and that both branch tips are ancestors of main's HEAD.
